## 1. The company

RINGS LUXURY is a HandCrafted haute joaillerie atelier founded by Jorge Uquillas, master
goldsmith and hand engraver. The atelier works with commissions only: every ring and necklace
is drawn for a single client, cast in solid 18k gold, engraved by hand and registered in the
atelier archive as one of one.

Ateliers: São Paulo (Avenida Paulista, Brazil) and Miami (Brickell, Florida, USA), both by
private appointment. Private video consultations for clients anywhere in the world.
Clients in 50+ countries.

Contact: +55 11 97724-0777 • uquillasartjewells@gmail.com • Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 19:00.
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ringsluxury

## 2. The maker

Jorge Uquillas is a master goldsmith and hand-engraver artist. His line of work runs from
hand engraving, the technique carried since Ancient Greek and Renaissance workshops, through
lost-wax casting, high-relief sculpting in gold, natural diamond setting and agate burnishing.
He holds the hand engraver himself: he does not outsource the engraving and he signs each piece.

He teaches the same discipline at the atelier academy, in a five-module program covering
design, artistic engraving fundamentals, the alchemy of metals, advanced gem setting and the
final masterpiece, taught directly by him (https://www.ringsluxuryart.com/courses).

## 3. Materials and technique

- Metal: solid 18k gold, 75% pure gold, cast, never plated. Rose, yellow and white gold
  alloys; platinum on commission.
- Hand engraving: 90 to 140 hours per ring, cut directly into the solid metal with
  tempered-steel hand gravers. Laser and machine engraving are not used.
- Stones: hand-selected natural diamonds, chosen for fire and structural quality, weighed and
  set one by one under the microscope, with prongs carved from the 18k gold itself.
  No lab-grown stones are used.
- Finishing: agate burnishing and hand polish, with a master hallmark micro-engraved in the metal.
- One of one: the original wax matrix is destroyed after casting, so no mould or replica of a
  client piece can ever be made.

## 4. The commission process

1. Private consultation, in person in São Paulo or Miami, or by video.
2. Design, metal, stones, price and timeline agreed in writing. Nothing is cast before
   written approval, and the ring size is taken before casting.
3. Payment in two stages: 50% to begin the work, 50% before shipping. Major credit cards in
   instalments, PIX or wire transfer, with discreet billing.
4. Production in 60 days, documented by photograph along the way.
5. Insured delivery, with the archival folio, certificate of authenticity and hallmark.

## 5. Documentation and provenance

Every piece leaves the atelier with:
- an archival folio, sealed, registering the piece in the atelier archive;
- a certificate of authenticity;
- the atelier master hallmark, micro-engraved in the metal itself;
- photographs of the finished piece and of the hallmark.

Because the wax matrix is destroyed after casting, provenance is physical, not documentary only.

## 6. Shipping and warranty

Fully insured door-to-door delivery worldwide, tracked with mandatory signature, in a
hand-worked varnished wooden presentation box inside neutral outer packaging. Shipping is
included on commissions above US$ 5,000. Damage or loss must be reported within 7 days with
photographs; the atelier files the claim with carrier and insurer.

Lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects in the metal, the hand engraving and the
settings, plus one hand polish per year by appointment. Normal wear from daily use is not a
defect. Micro-adjustments and additional engraving are quoted after inspection.

A finished 1/1 piece cannot be returned or resold, because no identical piece can be
reproduced. This is stated in writing before any payment. Manufacturing defects are always
repaired or remade at no cost.

## 7. Care

Store the piece in its case. Keep perfume and chemicals off the metal. Clean only with the
atelier dry flannel. Book the yearly atelier polish and have the settings checked under
magnification. Never machine-buff a hand-engraved ring: aggressive polishing rounds the crisp
classical edges the hand engraver created.

## 8. Diamonds: how to tell real from fake

Seven tests, with atelier photographs on
https://www.ringsluxuryart.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-your-diamonds-are-real-or-fake

1. Fog test. A real diamond disperses heat instantly and clears in 1 to 2 seconds. CZ, glass
   and moissanite hold the fog for 4 to 5 seconds.
2. 10x loupe. A natural diamond shows razor-sharp facet edges and tiny natural inclusions.
   CZ looks too perfect with rounded edges; moissanite shows double facet lines when tilted.
3. Weight against size. A cubic zirconia of the same diameter weighs about 1.7 times more
   than a real diamond.
4. UV fluorescence. About 25 to 35 percent of natural diamonds glow blue under long-wave UV,
   from trace elements formed over billions of years. No glow does not mean fake.
5. Diamond tester. It measures thermal conductivity and beeps instantly on a real diamond.
   Old single-probe testers can confuse moissanite with diamond; use a model that also measures
   electrical conductivity.
6. Water, newspaper and sparkle screening. A real diamond sinks fast, scrambles printed text
   beneath it, and shows white brilliance, rainbow fire and dark scintillation contrast at once.
7. Jeweler verdict. Only a microscope, a refractometer and a multi-tester separate natural
   diamond, lab-grown diamond and moissanite. Lab-grown stones pass every home test.

The 4Cs: cut decides the fire of the stone; colour grades how white it is; clarity grades
natural inclusions; carat is weight, not size alone.
